dedupe_keys.name: paying for the victorian desalination plant a case study in regulatory ambiguity essential services commission 2013

description: This conference paper by the chairperson of Victoria's economic regulator for water tells how the Millennium Drought and the failure of the spring break rains in 2006 and 2007 took Melbourne's storages from about 60 percent in January 2006 to below 30 percent by May 2007, with restrictions tightened every few months, and how that led to the Victorian desalination plant. Its main subject is the 2013 price review, in which the regulator had to decide how the plant's costs would be recovered, and it sets out the differing views of Melbourne Water, customers and the regulator and concludes the ambiguity must be settled before the issue is revisited in 2016. Coverage: one city and one regulatory decision, in narrative form. Access: a free PDF; the licence is not stated, and the author's opinions are personal. Caveats: written from the regulator's viewpoint, with the cost figures not read on the pages examined. It supports desalination and supply augmentation investment appraisal and tariff studies, and relates to the Singapore four national taps and Cape Town drought case studies in the catalogue.
